_comment: Station facts: everything particular to YOUR receivers, rig and measured limits.
Edit this file. Keys starting with an underscore are notes and are ignored.
The values shipped here are generic starting points: one R820T-class dongle (most RTL-SDRs) and one E4000.
Run `marsad config` to see what is loaded and from where.
_rtl_sdr_dir: Folder holding rtl_power.exe etc., relative to this file. Searched before PATH.
_rtl_power_exe: Optional. Which rtl_power to run: a name ("rtl_power" picks the stock build on purpose) or a path relative to this file. Unset, marsad runs rtl_power_gainfix when it is installed (packaging/rtl_power_gainfix/BUILD.md: it keeps the R820T/R860 gain and does not overflow on strong carriers) and the stock rtl_power with a warning when it is not.
_location: Set once to record outdoor weather (Open-Meteo, no key) and the sun's elevation in every sidecar's auto_conditions, e.g. {"location": {"lat": 51.48, "lon": -0.01}} in decimal degrees, in station.local.json beside station.json (git ignores it, so your position stays off GitHub; it is laid over this file when marsad loads), west and south negative. Two decimals (~1 km) is plenty. Without it those parts record the reason instead.
_retune_ms_per_hop_fftw: rtl_power_fftw overhead per hop: 59 ms (retune + first read) and 16 ms per extra 1.6 MB buffer read within a hop, built into marsad as a starting figure. Set retune_ms_per_hop_fftw and read_ms_per_buffer_fftw here to override.
_retune_ms_per_hop: Time rtl_power loses retuning between hops. It depends on the USB stack: run `marsad calibrate-retune --save` to measure yours.
_default_receiver: The receiver a command means when none is named. Unset, the first one listed below.

r820t.label: RTL-SDR with an R820T / R820T2 / R860 tuner (low-IF)

e4000.label: RTL-SDR with an Elonics E4000 tuner (zero-IF)
e4000._gaps_mhz: Nominal E4000 PLL lock gap. It varies per unit and moves with temperature: measure yours with rtl_test -t.

_receivers: Name them what you like; the name goes in each survey's fingerprint. device = USB index as rtl_test lists them, which is not guaranteed across replugs. tuner picks the gain ladder.
_spur_families_mhz: Harmonic families the analyser tags automatically. Order matters: tags are written in this order. Changing the list changes every peaks.csv, so do it between comparison sets, not inside one.
_readout_families_mhz: Families the live view names when you hover a line. An RTL2832U's clock harmonics fall on 14.4 MHz multiples, odd ones included.
_detection_floor_db: Smallest change compare-runs believes, by whether the hardware was touched between runs. Starting figures: repeat a run with nothing touched, and with the dongle moved, to measure your own.

fm.note: Broadcast FM: strong, always there, a quick check that the antenna works

adsb.note: ADS-B at 1090 MHz, also a positive control for the receive path

LS.note: E4000 only: nominal PLL gap to rtl_power's 2147.48 MHz ceiling

top.note: E4000 only: 2147-2187 MHz, above rtl_power's 2^31 ceiling; 22 hops of 2.4 MHz, 18.75 kHz bins

h1.note: hydrogen line, one hop centred on 1420.4058 MHz, 1.17 kHz bins, 60 s per spectrum; --baseline FILE for an off-source spectrum

_presets: Named ranges for `marsad run <preset> <duration>`. Keep `custom` so a hand-built range is recorded as custom rather than masquerading as a preset.
_builder_profiles: Extra named profiles the scan builder offers; they emit `custom` to the CLI. Example: {"baseline": {"lo": 700, "hi": 1700, "bin": 50, "gain": 29.7, "integ": 120, "dur": [1, "h"], "fw": 0, "as": "custom", "note": "one settings profile for every step of a chain test"}}.
_known_mhz: What is known to be in the band. Shown by the scan builder for whatever range is selected; add what you find. k = bad | spur | (plain).

builder_notes.title: 350 MHz
builder_notes.text: The E4000 switches between its VHF and UHF inputs at 350.0 MHz, which puts a step in the floor. Never read a level across it as a change in the sky.

builder_notes.title: Warm-up
builder_notes.text: The E4000's whole PLL range slides down as it warms, by 10-20 MHz over an hour of streaming, so the top hops can lock cold and drop out one at a time. Compare rtl_test -t cold and warm on your unit.

builder_notes.title: 1090 MHz
builder_notes.text: A warm E4000's PLL gap can reach 1090 MHz, and rtl_adsb keeps running through 'PLL not locked' with no clear error. Compare rtl_test -t cold and warm on your unit.

_builder_notes: Warnings the scan builder shows when a scan matches. when (all must hold): rx, tuner, engine (true = rtl_power_fftw), span [lo, hi] overlaps the scan, includes MHz, hi_above, hi_at_most, gain_above, gain_not, not_load, skip_below (warm-up discard under N min), chain_has / chain_lacks (regex on the chain text), module_on (a chain module id), preset, rx_not, exact [lo, hi].
_chain_modules: The physical rig, in signal order, for the scan builder. The source and the SDR are always present; the rest can be unchecked. enclosures: the three choices the builder's buttons offer for the SDR; enclosure_default: which one each receiver starts on (default the first).
_chain_labels: Standard names for parts in the Chain tab's palette, by part type, e.g. {"lna": "Bias-tee LNA"}.
_probe: Near-field Probe tab, all optional: targets (the devices offered), states, probes, durations_min, attenuators_db, chain_tail (the chain after the probe, by receiver). A probe straight onto a dongle whose bias-tee is on would short it; put a DC block in the chain.
_recorder: marsad watch. pool: folder for captures, relative to this file or absolute; pool_gb and daily_gb are soft caps, nothing is ever deleted - when full, events are still catalogued and fingerprinted but no IQ is written. roles: {"surveyor": name, "recorder": name}, which receiver does what in `watch survey` (default the first two receivers). serials: which dongle is which receiver, matched by serial number, e.g. {"r820t": "00000001"}; optional with one dongle, needed when two share a tuner type. ppm: each radio's measured frequency error by serial (reported minus true, per million), 0 until measured. band_tiers: first matching row wins; anything not listed is open. A private band NEVER has its raw IQ written to disk - only a 20 ms x 1 kHz power spectrogram, flagged PRIVATE: do not decode. The table shipped here follows North American allocations: if you are elsewhere, add your own cellular, paging, cordless and land-mobile bands before recording. reference_carriers_mhz: steady known carriers you choose, captured once a day, and never treated as clock artefacts.
_defaults: Last-used answers to the sidecar questions. `marsad run` rewrites this section after every run; everything else in this file is left alone.
